question_text:
Consider a copper-zinc corrosion couple. If the current density at the copper cathode is $0.05 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{cm}^2$, calculate the weight loss of zinc per hour if (1) the copper cathode area is $100 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ and the zinc anode area is $1 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ and (2) the copper cathode area is $1 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ and the zinc anode area is $100 \mathrm{~cm}^2$.

Give your answer as a tuple: (weight_loss_small_anode, weight_loss_large_anode).The units of each required answer are (g/h, g/h), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

In a galvanic corrosion couple, the total current is conserved: the current flowing at the copper cathode equals the current flowing at the zinc anode.

**Given:** Copper cathode current density $i_{\text{Cu}} = 0.05\ \text{A/cm}^2$

The total corrosion current is determined by the cathode:
$$I = i_{\text{Cu}} \times A_{\text{Cu}}$$

This same current drives zinc dissolution at the anode. Weight loss via Faraday's law:
$$\Delta m = \frac{I \cdot t \cdot M_{\text{Zn}}}{n \cdot F},\quad M_{\text{Zn}}=65.38\ \text{g/mol},\ n=2,\ F=96485\ \text{C/mol},\ t=3600\ \text{s}$$

**Case (1):** $A_{\text{Cu}}=100\ \text{cm}^2$ (small Zn anode $=1\ \text{cm}^2$)
$$I = 0.05 \times 100 = 5\ \text{A}$$
$$\Delta m_1 = \frac{5 \times 3600 \times 65.38}{2 \times 96485} \approx 6.10\ \text{g/h}$$

**Case (2):** $A_{\text{Cu}}=1\ \text{cm}^2$ (large Zn anode $=100\ \text{cm}^2$)
$$I = 0.05 \times 1 = 0.05\ \text{A}$$
$$\Delta m_2 = \frac{0.05 \times 3600 \times 65.38}{2 \times 96485} \approx 0.0610\ \text{g/h}$$

This illustrates the **area effect**: a small anode coupled to a large cathode suffers dramatically higher weight loss (100× more here), since the same total current is funneled through less anode area.

$$\boxed{(6.10,\ 0.0610)}$$
